newsitem.title: INDIA: Agriculture gets top priority in India's 9th plan.
newsitem.headline: Agriculture gets top priority in India's 9th plan.

text.p: India's Planning Commission said on Friday that agriculture was crucial to the nation's overall economic growth and would receive top priority in the country's ninth economic plan covering the next five years.

"The plan has given highest priority to agriculture and rural development with a view to generate productive employment and poverty alleviation," Madhu Dandavate, deputy chairman of Planning Commission, told a news conference.
The ninth plan will begin on April 1 and run until 2002.
Dandvate reiterated that the broad economic blueprint for the period 1997-2002 would target seven percent growth in gross domestic product (GDP).
The agricultural sector employs 65 percent of the country's workforce and accounts for 35 percent of GDP, he said.
The ninth plan aims to achieve growth of 4.5 percent in agriculture, up from a target of 3.5 percent set in an early draft, he said.
Dandavate said the Planning Commission estimated 37 percent of India's 930 million people were living below the poverty line.
He said the government should offer incentives to increase farm exports and boost agriculture growth rate.
"Unless agricultural growth complements and supplements the rate of growth in industry it is not possible to reach the targeted growth of seven percent of GDP," Dandavate said.
He said the National Development Council, which includes all state chief ministers, unanimously approved on Thursday the panel's target of seven percent annual economic growth.
Dandavate said the growth rate target, set at 5.9 percent in the eighth plan, could be increased by stepping up savings, investment and efficient use of funds invested in the economy.
